ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a transition-state structure containing a fused bicyclic organic skeleton: the left side is a six-membered carbon ring, and the right side is an N-containing six-membered ring; there is a positive charge mark near the middle, and there are curved arrows. Below/lower right of the structure there are substituents R and OPOCl2, and at the lower left there is also a free Cl−. The figure also has hydrogen-related labels such as N–H and C–H. Reasoning: According to the question and method requirements, ignore all arrows and do not count any bonds involving H. First count the heavy-atom connections of the fused bicyclic core: the left six-membered ring and the right N-containing ring share one bond in the middle, giving a total of 11 unique heavy-atom bond connections. Then count the heavy-atom bonds of the substituents and internal groups: central carbon–R is 1, central carbon–O is 1, O–P is 1, P=O is 1, and the two P–Cl bonds are 2. Free Cl− does not form a bond and contributes 0. Therefore the total is 11 + 6 = 17.

method.method_draft: Ignore all arrows and all bonds to H. Count heavy-atom bond connections region by region: the fused bicyclic core has 11 unique heavy-atom connections, obtained from the left six-membered ring plus the right N-containing ring with their shared central bond counted only once. Then count substituent/internal group bonds: central carbon-R = 1, central carbon-O = 1, O-P = 1, P=O = 1, and two P-Cl bonds = 2. The free Cl− contributes 0 bonds. Sum 11 + 6 = 17.

method.method_draft: Make an adjacency count of unique non-H bonds. First list the fused-ring graph edges: six around the left ring and six around the right heterocycle, subtracting the one central shared edge, giving 6 + 6 - 1 = 11. Then add graph edges outside the ring system: one C-R edge and five edges belonging to the phosphate chloride substituent path/branches, namely C-O, O-P, P=O, P-Cl, and P-Cl. Do not add anything for N-H, C-H, arrows, or free Cl−. The graph-edge total is 11 + 1 + 5 = 17.
